The plan's pinned Lean Challenge Statement for stepOk/stepOk_sound types the world argument as World (Fin 4) (LS (Fin 4) Nat) (Msg Nat). That signature is UNIMPLEMENTABLE: Distsys.Exec.Net N M = Packet N M -> Prop has no Decidable instance, so deliver's w.net.mem p premise cannot be decided from a World. The same plan's Decision 4 and report 02 Finding 3 say the opposite -- 'an executable SimWorld mirror with an abstraction into World, NOT decide over World'. The two are in direct conflict; Decision 4 was followed and stepOk takes the mirror, with the pinned CONCLUSION recovered unchanged at ew.toWorld. Nothing is weakened, but the pinned block's argument type is departed from and needs a user ruling.

Distsys.Bracha.applyLabel, which the plan's pinned stepOk_sound names as the successor-world function, is the IDENTITY on .env (.drop _), .env (.duplicate _) and .env (.corrupt _ _) -- its own book needed only the inject case. The plan's run 2 (crash below the bound) drops a crashed node's in-flight packets, so a checker stated over that applier could never accept it. Resolution: a checker-local total applier Distsys.Replay.applyLbl that agrees with Bracha.applyLabel wherever that one is not identity-on-env (proved as applyLbl_eq_applyLabel) and additionally pins the three further byzAllowed cases that ARE deterministic. tamper, the only nondeterministic action, stays outside the alphabet.

The task description's own framing of the question this task answers is now partly obsolete, and the plan had to reframe it rather than follow it literally. The description treats MAX_CHUNKS=50 drain rate as the binding constraint and names 'extraction spends real money or CPU per run' only as a caveat against backgroundSync. Post-migration the live numbers invert that: one 50-chunk pass staged 1208 knowledge objects against a 2000 objects/day cap (so ~60 percent of a day's cap in a single pass), took 29 minutes rather than seconds, left 1208 objects in an unreviewed queue, and is billed per call to the user's Anthropic key. The backlog it drains is small by comparison (78 'would ingest now' of 1153 on disk). The binding constraints are now the daily object cap, the review-queue depth, and per-pass cost -- not the chunk cap.

Found a latent, separate throttle in the Sapience vendor client (~/.sapience/extract_local.py ollama_num_thread(), comment references 'Ari Sklar #12, 2026-09-19'): the scheduled --sync path (SYNC and not BACKFILL) defaults num_thread to 1 deliberately so a background cron-style run never takes every core; only an interactive run or --backfill gets Ollama's own default (unset/0, effectively all cores). This is unrelated to the measured 0.66 tok/s event (that event's own llama-server log line shows n_threads_batch=24, i.e. not single-threaded) but must be accounted for before treating any local-sync throughput number as representative, and would need a deliberate override (SAPIENCE_NUM_THREAD or config.json num_thread) if local sync inference is ever made the default path.
